elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph opens "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Contractor shall ...", so all three obligations attach to every expiry and every termination, including under 6(a) and 6(b).

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: "(i) at Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months" — Contractor (Vendor) is the obligated party and the period is six months.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: "... for up to six (6) months at Contractor's then-current rates".

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "(ii) within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination, return all data and materials belonging to, supplied by or processed for Company (\"Company Data\")" — the 30-day clock runs from expiry/termination, not from a request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Return is "in a standard machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: "(iii) after such return, delete all Company Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing to Company" — deletion and certification are expressly sequenced after return.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same inserted trigger language: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Up to six (6) months of transition assistance exceeds the 90-day fallback floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Return of all Company Data in a standard machine-readable format within thirty (30) days after expiry or termination satisfies the export requirement.

reasons: The finding is correctly classified as missing: Section 6(a)-(c) addresses only notice-based termination, final fees and assignment of Works in progress, and no other cited provision requires transition help, data return or deletion.

All six preferred elements are carried in a single inserted wind-down paragraph, so the preferred level is position-complete; the fallback is satisfied a fortiori (six months > 90 days; 30-day return).

Minimal: one concise insertion into the existing termination section, no deletions, no paraphrase of retained language, and no extras beyond the checklist (no survival tail, no at-own-expense or additional remedies language). The inline definition of "Company Data" is necessary because the Agreement does not otherwise define the data category, and it covers all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Company rather than selected named types.

Preserves intent: the retained final-payment and Works-in-progress mechanics in 6(b) and the stray 6(c) survive without contradiction, and the new paragraph creates no dangling cross-reference or undefined term.

Drafting nit only (not a defect in operative effect): the new paragraph is unlettered and sits between 6(b) and 6(c); consider lettering it (e.g., as a new 6(c) with renumbering, or 6(d)) so it cannot be read as a subpart of the breach-termination provision. Its own opening words ("expiry or termination ... for any reason") already make its scope self-contained.
